However, the AI-authored sub-commit 92cef77e was a REFACTOR that moved the DeduplicationHandler from the cache interceptor to a standalone file. The vulnerable design pattern (unbounded `this.#chunks.push(Buffer.from(chunk))` + `Buffer.concat(this.#chunks)` without size limits) was introduced in the FIRST sub-commit c75c9c9e by Matteo Collina with NO AI signals (touched_blamed_file=false for that commit because it put the code in a different file path). The AI refactor merely moved the same vulnerable code to the blamed file without modifying the buffering logic. The vulnerability is a design-level omission (no size bounds on response buffering) that existed from the initial human-authored commit. For the other 4 vulnerabilities (CRLF, window bits, decompression bomb, 64-bit overflow, duplicate headers), all origin commits are by human contributors (Khafra, Robert Nagy, tsctx) with zero AI markers. The pipeline correctly found no AI signals on those BICs.

notes: This is a file-path attribution error. The blamed file (lib/handler/deduplication-handler.js) was CREATED by the AI-authored refactor commit, but the vulnerable code pattern within it originated from an earlier human-authored commit in a different file path. The pipeline's touched_blamed_file heuristic correctly identifies which decomposed commit created the blamed file, but cannot determine whether that commit introduced the vulnerability vs. merely relocated pre-existing vulnerable code. This is a known pipeline limitation (blame can't trace cross-file code moves, documented in MEMORY.md). The other 4+ vulnerabilities in this advisory are entirely human-authored with no AI involvement whatsoever.
